styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Gothic lanes, Gaudí landmarks and the old city on foot.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Markets, tapas bars and long lunches by the sea.

styles.label: Beach
styles.blurb: City beaches, a swim and seafood on the sand.

stays.why: Sleep in the medieval centre. Walk to the cathedral, La Rambla and the port. Can be noisy at night.
Grid streets with Modernista buildings. Good metro links and calmer nights than the old town.
Bars, boutiques and the Picasso Museum near the park. Lively but central and walkable.
Village feel with small squares and local restaurants. Quieter, a short metro ride from the sights.

food: Try Catalan dishes: pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato), escalivada and crema catalana.
La Boqueria market off La Rambla is busy and pricey; locals often shop at Santa Caterina or El Ninot instead.
Lunch is the big meal, often a fixed menú del dia around €12–20. Dinner starts late, often after 21:00.
Tapas bars in El Born and Gràcia are cheaper and calmer than the Rambla strip. Stand at the bar to pay less.
Book popular restaurants ahead. Many close one day a week and some shut in August; check on the day.
more_time: Swap a beach afternoon for Montjuïc: cable car, gardens and city views, then the Miró foundation.
Take a half-day train to Montserrat for the mountain monastery; check times and ticket options on the day.
Add a day trip to Girona or Sitges by train if you want a change from the city.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the Gothic quarter, Gaudí sights and a beach or Montjuïc afternoon without rushing.

month_notes: January: cold and quiet, highs near 14°C. Pack a warm layer; few crowds.
February: still cool, highs around 15°C, a few rainy days. Good for museums.
March: mild at 16°C with more showers. Bring a light rain jacket.
April: pleasant 18°C days, some rain. Great for walking the old town.
May: warm at 21°C and mostly dry. Beach days start to work.
June: hot at 26°C, warm evenings. Busy but not peak yet.
July: hot and dry, highs near 29°C. Book ahead and swim early or late.
August: hot and humid, highs near 29°C. Many locals leave; some shops close.
September: warm at 25°C but the wettest month, around 12 rain days. Keep plans flexible.
October: mild at 22°C with some rain. Comfortable for sightseeing.
November: cooler at 17°C, more showers. Fewer tourists.
December: cold at 15°C, few rain days. Festive lights and quiet sights.

climate_guide.summary: Mediterranean climate: mild winters, hot dry summers and the most rain in autumn.

items.title: Best time: May to July
items.text: Warm days around 21–29°C with little rain. Good for both sightseeing and the beach.

items.title: Hot summer (July and August)
items.text: Highs near 29°C and lows around 21–22°C. Sightsee early morning or evening; rest at midday.

items.title: Wettest in autumn
items.text: September has about 12 rain days and October about 10. Showers can be heavy; carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Mild but cool winters
items.text: January highs near 14°C and lows around 5°C. A warm coat is needed, especially at night.

items.title: Beach season
items.text: Comfortable swimming is roughly June to September. May and October are for walks, not long swims.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes and sunscreen for summer; a layer for cool evenings; a rain jacket for spring and autumn.

transit.best: Metro for most trips; walk the old town and use taxis late at night.

modes.text: Metro and FGC trains cover the city. Zone 1 tickets are cheap and contactless via T-mobilitat.
City and intercity buses fill the gaps. Night buses run when the metro closes.
Taxis are metered. Uber, Bolt and Cabify operate in Barcelona.
Driving is slow and parking is costly. Leave the car outside the centre.
Walking is best in the old town. Bike lanes and Bicing-style bike hire are common.
Ferries and cruise shuttles link the port to La Rambla and the Balearics.
